note: [agent-bulk] other_em, and a messy one: the whole event is a long dense column of charge with several near-parallel grey tracks running through it. shw 3012 (173.6 MeV, pdg 11, conn 1) has only TWO members and they cannot be one cone: 3012 (25.2 cm, the narrow straight line running off the X) and 3008 (25.8 cm) at dist 46.5 cm and angle 97.6 deg -- essentially perpendicular to the axis -- pulled in by pass3_cluster_map. Both azimuths show them as two separate objects at opposite ends of the column with the middle unclaimed. 3008 marked OUT. What I could NOT settle, and it may matter more than the verdict: cluster 3 is one big vertex complex of long prongs -- 3005 (28.5 cm pdg 2212) and 3009 (50.6 cm pdg 211) both touch 3012's start at dist 0 and are unowned, and 3004 (65 cm pdg 13), 3006 (73 cm pdg 2212), 3010/3011 (45.4/7.4 cm pdg 2212) sit 23-47 cm out -- so a second reading is that the segmentation of this whole region is arbitrary and 'over-clustered' understates it. I make no PID claim on 3012 itself, though its body is a straight narrow line rather than a cone. Vertex judged first and left alone: at el+60 the star is where a long thin track ends on the activity complex, which is a plausible convergence. Not judged individually: shw 72040 (181.1 MeV but pdg 13, 109.2 cm long -- a track-PID object whose 10 extra members are a cluster-73 spray at 12.7-44.4 deg, which would need its own look) and shw 68030 (20.8 MeV, 5.7 cm); 17 further showers skipped by the scope rule, all at 15.0 MeV and below. pi0: the reco accepted no group, but the display prices 3012+68030 at 107.1 MeV (axis) / 86.6 MeV (vertex), both inside the code's accept window. I do NOT store that pairing -- 3012's own membership is what I just disputed, so its energy is not the one that pairing should be priced with. Flagging it only as something the owner may want to re-price after the OUT mark.
